chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The taslīm in the two rakʿahs of al-watr?” He said: “It awakens the sleeper, and you may speak concerning a need.”

key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the watr prayer in the night prayer sequence
key_terms.بِالْحَاجَةِ: regarding a need or necessary matter

ai.seo_question: Does giving taslīm in the two rakʿahs before al-watr create a separating break that allows speaking?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates a legal distinction between the two rakʿahs connected with al-watr and what follows, such that taslīm is given in a way that marks separation. The Imam عليه السلام points to practical signs of that separation: it would awaken one who is asleep, and one may speak regarding a need.
